QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_78

question.text: Which of the following correctly describes how corporate actions affect equity derivative contracts?

answer.text: In equity derivatives, corporate actions such as bonus issues, stock splits, rights issues, and extraordinary dividends trigger adjustments to the strike price, position, and market lot or multiplier of the contract
Corporate actions affect all derivative markets equally
Only currency derivatives are affected by corporate actions through central bank actions
Corporate actions do not affect any derivative contracts

explanation.text: The Logic: When the underlying stock undergoes a corporate action such as a bonus issue, stock split, rights issue, or extraordinary dividend, the exchange adjusts the strike price, the open position, and the market lot or multiplier of the equity derivative contract so that the economic value of positions is preserved. The Trap: Saying that corporate actions affect all derivative markets equally, or that they do not affect any contracts at all, misstates the equity-specific adjustment framework. Note: Treat the adjustment rule strictly within equity derivatives; the source pages reviewed do not establish a corresponding corporate-action adjustment regime for currency or interest rate derivatives.
